title: When compiling with `module_tilemap_enabled=no` and running `doctest`, a few `GDScript` tests fail because they depend on `TileSet`
body:
### Tested versions

master [5902d3f370db5905444a01139722a40cb29bb1c4]
doctest [2.4.12]

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev2 - macOS Sequoia (15.7.5) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 (Apple9) - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

After #121548, I tried compiling with all unnecessary modules disabled so I can compile a smaller-sized dev-build editor. While running tests, though, these doctests will fail:


This doesn't affect editor builds or exports, of course, but I would prefer that the tests from one module or core don't fail, especially an important module as `GDScript`, just because I excluded other unrelated modules. (Sorta unrelated, but `tests/scene/test_generic_6dof_joint_3d.cpp` also fails when the 3D physics modules are excluded from compilation, and `tests/core/io/test_image.cpp` when the `exr` module is excluded, which also shouldn't happen in my opinion, but I think those can be fixed by just surrounding those certain tests with `#ifdef MODULE_*_ENABLED` directives, but this issue is the most pressing because enums aren't dependent on `TileSet`.)

### Steps to reproduce

* Compile godot with `module_tilemap_enabled=no` and `tests=yes` in master (or any branch that includes [a11d9ad]), making sure the `GDScript` module is still enabled ofc.
* Run `doctest` by suffixing with `--test` in command-line
* Notice the failures, especially `Could not find type "TileSet" in the current scope.` and `Identifier "TileSet" not declared in the current scope.`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I doubt it can be minimal or safe to upload the binary, even with every module other than `GDScript` disabled, and my binary won't work on everyone's computers (it's `godot.macos.editor.dev.arm64`).
